answer.rationale: While switching to the low-cost vendor previously succeeded (memory_c2), the assembly line’s 94% utilization with no buffer makes any vendor transition unacceptably risky. Renewing with the incumbent preserved integration stability across cycles (memory_c1), and prior negotiations at renewal recovered margin while benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and payment terms (memory_c4). Multi-year commitments with the incumbent have also unlocked volume pricing and cost reductions without narrowing service scope (memory_c6). Therefore, negotiating terms with the incumbent using the low-cost vendor’s quote as leverage is the optimal path to meet the 18% cost reduction mandate without increasing delivery risk. Verifying memory_c4 will confirm the specifics of prior successful negotiations to strengthen the approach.
